text.paragraph: Three-month review: A1c, lipids, walking program, eye treatment, and foot care. [S]

Ms. Fitzgerald returns three months after her first visit, after a two-week run of concerts. She completed ten weeks of the supervised exercise program and walked to the home plan on tour; she can now walk about three blocks before calf pain, and the pain eases faster. She has had three right-eye injections, and her right eye is clearer. The podiatrist pared her calluses and she now performs in low-heeled custom stage shoes. Her glucose monitor shows time in range 66% and time below 70 mg/dL 0.8%, with no reading below 54 mg/dL; she ate before every late show. She has had no bleeding on rivaroxaban and aspirin. Her hepatitis C screening test was negative. She would like to know whether anything else can help her legs and her glucose. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-10; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 82.1 kg, BMI 30.2; blood pressure 122/68, pulse 62
Skin intact; small calluses; hammer toes; no ulcer; monofilament felt at all sites; right foot pulses absent, left faint; shoes fit well
Best-corrected acuity 71 letters right and 81 letters left

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral artery disease: cramping in both calves after about one and a half blocks of walking, worse on the right, easing within minutes of rest; no rest pain, wounds, or color change. Resting ankle-brachial index 0.62 right and 0.74 left, toe-brachial index 0.46 and 0.55; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent on the right and faint on the left. A1c 8.6% on metformin, glipizide and glargine, with low glucose readings (to 52 mg/dL) after late performances. Foot: protective sensation intact to the 10-g monofilament at all sites and to vibration; callus under the second metatarsal heads; hammer toes of the second and third toes; no ulcer (IWGDF risk category 2). Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetes and its circulatory complications
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the type of diabetes was not made public and is synthetic.

Moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy with center-involving diabetic macular edema in the right eye (best-corrected acuity 64 letters, about 20/50) and moderate nonproliferative retinopathy without macular edema in the left eye (81 letters); lens implants in both eyes from earlier cataract surgery. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetic eye problems
S — Synthetic modern eye diagnosis on retinal imaging and optical coherence tomography in the clinic; the left eye is described in the display.

Coronary artery disease after five-vessel coronary bypass surgery last year, with an intensive care stay; no angina now; on aspirin, a statin, and metoprolol. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented heart surgery
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented heart surgery; bypass grafts are described in the display.

list.item:
Type 2 diabetes with peripheral artery disease (E11.51). A1c 7.6%, from 8.6%, without level 2 lows; still just above her goal below 7.5%. Walking distance has doubled with supervised exercise. With coronary and peripheral artery disease, a GLP-1 receptor agonist adds cardiovascular protection, and in people with peripheral artery disease and type 2 diabetes semaglutide has increased walking distance. Because a fast fall in glucose can briefly worsen retinopathy, the retina clinic was told before the start and the dose will rise slowly. Creatinine 0.96 mg/dL and eGFR 64, a small expected change on empagliflozin; potassium 4.6 mmol/L. [S]
Start semaglutide 0.25 mg weekly for four weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly.
Eat smaller meals and stop eating when full; call for persistent vomiting or abdominal pain.
Continue glargine 24 units; lower it if fasting readings fall below 90 mg/dL.
Finish the twelve weeks of supervised exercise, then walk at least three times a week.

Coronary artery disease after bypass surgery (I25.10). LDL 64 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg, above the goal below 55 mg/dL; HDL 46 and triglycerides 112 mg/dL. No angina. [S]
Add ezetimibe 10 mg daily.
Lipid panel in 4 to 12 weeks.

Diabetic macular edema, right eye (E11.3311). Acuity 71 letters, from 64, after three injections; the retina clinic will now lengthen the interval. [S]
Continue retina-clinic treatment.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); Practical guidelines on the prevention and management of diabetes-related foot disease (IWGDF 2023 update) (2023); 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (2024); 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026); Semaglutide and walking capacity in people with symptomatic peripheral artery disease and type 2 diabetes (STRIDE): a phase 3b, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (2025)

Follow-up: Semaglutide dose step in four weeks, by video visit if she is touring. Podiatry in September. Review in eleven weeks with A1c, lipids, and kidney tests; zoster vaccine dose 1 at that visit. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-26: five-and-a-half-month review: A1c, lipids, walking distance, revascularization decision, foot and eye follow-up. [S]
